claims.text: Machine learning-based molecular dynamics simulations can be used to design and optimize the microstructure of high-entropy alloys.
Optimizing HEA microstructures using machine learning-based molecular dynamics can produce ultrahigh strength and ductility.
The proposed method can overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
Relevant HEA microstructural variables include grain size, precipitation structures, and alloy composition.
Machine learning-based molecular dynamics simulations can identify promising HEA compositions.
Machine learning-based molecular dynamics simulations can identify promising processing techniques.
Machine learning-based molecular dynamics simulations can reveal mechanisms governing the strength-ductility trade-off.
Dislocation glide, grain-boundary sliding, and precipitation hardening are mechanisms controlling the strength-ductility trade-off in HEAs.
Conventional material processing approaches reduce ductility when strength is increased.
The extent to which machine learning-based molecular dynamics can improve HEA strength and ductility is uncertain and requires further research.
